A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ViEEG framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite the changed title and organization.

before.justification: v1 reports original THINGS-EEG recognition experiments, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, retrieval results, and image reconstructions.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds THINGS-MEG experiments, encoder and processing-order ablations, reconstruction metrics, and timing measurements.

M1.justification: The proposed image decomposition, three EEG encoders, hierarchical cross-attention, concatenated contrastive objective, and SDXL/IP-Adapter reconstruction pipeline remain unchanged. The added encoder and ordering variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates THINGS-EEG only. v3 additionally evaluates 200-way recognition on THINGS-MEG with four participants, extending coverage to another neural recording modality and participant population. Retrieval and reconstruction tasks already existed in v1.

E2.justification: The ten baselines in the main EEG comparison are retained. v3 adds six encoder-replacement comparators within the hierarchical framework (Table 7) and reconstruction comparisons against NICE, ATM, and CogCap (Table 10), substantially broadening the comparative evaluation.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a subject-dependent MEG protocol, encoder/order controls, seven reconstruction metrics, and timing evaluations. Appendix 6.1 also changes reported EEG downsampling from 100 to 250 Hz and test-image repetitions from one to 80, although Section 4.1 still specifies 100 Hz. These are documentation-level protocol revisions; the PDFs do not establish that the retained EEG experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds encoder substitutions to examine whether performance depends on ViEEG's encoder rather than segmentation alone, and tests five alternative hierarchical processing orders (Tables 7–8). The existing embedding, cross-attention, and attention-depth/head analyses are retained, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify five repetitions and report mean accuracy without seed identifiers, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or formal significance tests. The new results retain point-estimate reporting; v3 explicitly states that statistical analysis was not conducted for MEG.

E6.justification: The numerical entries in retained EEG Tables 2, 3, 5, and 6 are unchanged, including ViEEG's 40.9% subject-dependent and 22.9% subject-independent Top-1 accuracy. v3 adds MEG results of 25.5%/63.2% Top-1/Top-5, encoder/order results, reconstruction scores such as SSIM 0.356, and training/inference timings. These are additional results, not improvements over v1 under the same settings.

T1.justification: The task formulation and mathematical operations in Equations 1–11 are retained. Changes such as replacing initial-feature notation and explaining LayerNorm do not alter the mathematics. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The hierarchy-neglect diagnosis, tri-stream architecture, biological motivation, and main EEG performance claims remain. v3's abstract and conclusion additionally claim generalization to MEG and other neural modalities, extending the applicability claim without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive interpretations attributing performance to segmentation–encoder synergy, supporting the biological processing order, and linking reconstruction gains to EEG–CLIP alignment under a shared diffusion model. It expands deployment-efficiency arguments and qualifies MEG evidence because of its small participant count. Existing reconstruction failures and their speculative explanations remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds EEG demographic, referencing, and target-trial handling details, documents MEG acquisition/preprocessing, and reports training/test times. It also replaces the bigG checkpoint pointer with an H/14 pointer matching the stated backbone. Core hardware, optimizer, and training hyperparameters remain unchanged; the conflicting sampling descriptions limit reproducibility.

R1.justification: v3 adds the THINGS and THINGS-data references, Liu et al. 2025, and a complete BiRefNet citation, while removing the neural-speech reference with the condensed multimodal discussion. The central positioning against flat EEG representations remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 retitles and substantially reorganizes the document: preliminaries move into Method, the separate Discussion is absorbed into Experiment, and related work is condensed. The appendices switch from lettered sections to a reorganized numerical sequence, with expanded dataset and computational-efficiency prose.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document template, relocates the opening figures, enlarges appendix displays, adds MEG/encoder/order/reconstruction tables, and redesigns the resource table with timing columns. The redundant recognition-summary table and compact main-text parameter plot disappear, while their underlying information remains elsewhere.

improvement.justification: The encoder and ordering controls better distinguish architectural contributions from segmented-image supervision, while Table 10 adds quantitative evidence for previously qualitative reconstruction claims. These improve empirical support. However, conflicting EEG sampling rates, inconsistent MEG training-versus-held-out concept counts, and absent uncertainty estimates limit confidence in the expanded evaluation, making the net quality improvement modest.
